title: The Hand That Sorts the Cards
description: Michel de Certeau’s tactics reveal why frontier LLMs are never neutral tools: every workaround users invent inside a platform’s ‘proper place’ can be captured, generalized, or closed off.

title: Who Pays When AI Is Wrong?
description: AI can loosen authorship without loosening accountability: the person who signs an output may lose credit for producing it yet become the system’s moral crumple zone when it fails.

title: No Clean Slate
description: Failed rollouts do more than create scepticism: they teach employees that action is futile, turning the next AI initiative — however sound — into a test of trust already depleted.

title: All the Unwritten Processes
description: Every agent roadmap begins with work it cannot see: people translate tacit practice into legible inputs, then absorb the exceptions, repairs, and coordination that keep automation running.

title: The Ghost Competence
description: Automation can make a workforce look more capable while preventing competence from forming: people inherit outputs without the judgment, calibrated trust, or ability to take back control.

title: Briefing Is Not Chatting
description: Chat narrowed the skills gap by supplying answers. Agents widen it again: they reward those who can turn ambiguous work into briefs, constraints, and evaluable sequences.

title: The Articulation Gap
description: The AI super-user is less a technical type than the visible beneficiary of Bourdieu’s linguistic capital: LLMs reward the ability to formulate, frame, and judge — then turn class advantage into performance.

title: Who Is Conducting Whom?
description: AI does not simply extend thought; it changes the plane on which thought moves, opening fast, rhizomatic exploration while weakening the intuitive ground that lets us know where we are.

title: The Human Bottleneck
description: Agentic AI removes the machine bottleneck only to expose another: the finite human capacity to set direction, retain context, verify outputs, and decide what deserves trust.

title: The people in the middle of GenAI adoption
description: GenAI adoption is not a technology problem with a training solution. It is a social adoption problem, carried by the people between leadership and frontline peers whose trust and professional identity determine whether use sticks.

title: When Feedback Fails
description: Feedback is not a free good: more than a third of interventions lower performance, making the design of the system — not good intentions — the real management problem.

title: When the Train Comes Off the Tracks
description: Underperformance triggers control; control makes honest information costly; the organisation then loses the very signals it needs to understand the decline.
